items.title: Why California Electricity Bills Surged
items.summary:
California power rates have gone up. Why?

Heron Power CEO Drew Baglino gives 3 reasons:

1. Wildfire abatement costs and liability from past fires

2. Rising costs of the components needed to maintain and build out the grid

3. Most controversial: net energy metering. Homeowners with solar used to get paid full retail price for excess power they sent back to the grid, even though it costs the utility less to buy that power than to deliver it to a home.

That's since changed, and Drew thinks rates could actually start coming down from here.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: OpenAI's 9-Month Chip Beats Nvidia on Inference and Jensen Should Be Worried

Designed specifically for internal inference workloads, Jalapeño leverages Codex and Google's XLS compilers to automate lower-level RTL coding and hardware abstractions. While early benchmarks from SemiAnalysis suggest high token-output efficiency, Jalapeño is not a general-purpose GPU meant to replace Nvidia's training dominance; rather, it is a strategic FinOps move to optimise token costs and bypass global data centre power bottlenecks.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Senior Tech Journalist Supreeth Koundinya to analyse OpenAI's custom hardware strategy. They discuss the realities of AI-assisted chip design, why inference ASICs are replacing general-purpose GPUs for enterprise token delivery, analysing the benchmark claims against Nvidia, and what India's Semiconductor Mission 2.0 can learn from global partnership models.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Two Indian Space Founders Who Met Modi Reveal What He Said in the Room

Six years after opening the space sector to private participation, India is home to nearly 440 registered space tech startups. As ISRO transfers mature technologies like SSLV and PSLV to private industry, the sector is shifting from basic launch vehicles toward specialised downstream applications and active space debris removal.

He describes how DBT allows users to break down complex transformations into modest SQL select statements, forming a directed acyclic graph (DAG) that makes data modeling simple and scalable. This process ensures that data consumed by BI tools or analytics agents is nicely modeled and readily available.
